" U.S. Drug Czar Warns Canada on Plan "
By THE ASSOCIATED PRESS
(MarijuanaNews note: Plan?? The Canadian Press had a very similar article with the headline " U.S. Drug Czar Visits Canada and Preaches Tougher War Against Pot. "

This is a pretty good article, which means that it is unlikely to be printed in many DEAland papers. So far, I have not found the CP article in any major Canadian papers. I expect that it may inspire a few editorials, however.

The Globe and Mail, one of Canada's two national papers, did carry a web report that Walters met with the Canadian Senate Special Committee on Illegal Drugs, which is looking at the cannabis issue in Canada.

Committee chair Pierre Claude Nolin said that Canada needs to include the United States in discussions on the creation of a new drug policy.

Walters told the group that if Canada adopts some form of decriminalization of marijuana, the U.S. would not want to encroach on Canada's legislation.

How droll of the Senator! He knows very well that Walters would choke if told the truth.)

QUEBEC (AP) -- Canada should get tough on marijuana instead of decriminalizing the drug or allowing people to use it for medicinal purposes, U.S. drug policy chief John Walters said Wednesday.

" Canada's decision about how it handles this or other issues of regulated substance is its decision. We respect that,'' Walters told reporters during a two-day visit for an international meeting of the College on Problems of Drug Dependence.

But he made it clear the American government disagrees with recent moves in Canada to liberalize drug policies.

More than 250 Canadians have federal government clearance to smoke marijuana for medical reasons. Canada amended drug laws last year to allow patients with conditions such as HIV, cancer, and multiple sclerosis to use marijuana legally.
See

Walters said there were better ways to treat patients than smoking marijuana.
See

A Canadian Senate committee has expressed initial support for decriminalizing marijuana, with its final report due in August following public hearings. A preliminary report released in May said no scientific evidence exists that marijuana use leads to harder drugs, or that it is more dangerous to society than alcohol.
See

Canadian federal agencies spend about $326 million each year to fight drugs and more than 30,000 people are charged with simple possession annually, the preliminary report said.
(MarijuanaNews note: The population of Canada is 30 million, a little more than 10% of DEAland's, so it is arresting less than half as many people per capita on marijuana charges as DEAland. Canada also spends far less per capita on its drug war than does DEAland. The Drug Czar's office has a budget of almost $20 billion.

In fact, there were far fewer marijuana arrests in Canada last year than in New York City, which has a population of only 7 million.
See

By the way, a little good news from New York: the latest attempt to reform New York's so-called Rockefeller drug laws no longer includes Governor Pataki's effort to link reform to harsher penalties for marijuana possession.)

If Canada follows the committee's initial recommendations, marijuana would still be illegal, but users would not be penalized. That would differ from the zero tolerance policy of the U.S. government.

Walters, the director of the White House Office of National Drug Control Policy, said that of the 4.3 million Americans suffering drug addiction, 65 percent are dependent on marijuana.

(MarijuanaNews note: And now for the punch line.)

Liberal drug laws in Canada would be a concern for the United States, Walters said.

" It certainly could become a problem if the trade is able to use our borders as a vehicle to enhance their effectiveness to move drugs across the border,'' he said of drug smugglers.

(MarijuanaNews note: So, what does all this mean?

It is very good that Walters met with the Canadian Senate committee. And it is certainly " good news " that he has given explicit permission for Canada to act like a sovereign nation and make its own laws. But what else could he say?

The " bad news " is that most of the Senators know that Walters is a liar, so they don't necessarily take his statement at face value.

The fact is that Canada is not going to be a major supplier of any illegal drugs going into DEAland.

But that is not the party line, so any move to restore freedom to Canadians will continue to be met with howls of protest, because changes in Canada's cannabis laws would be a political threat to DEAland prohibition.

Of course, the DEAland can also count on continued support from Canadian collaborators in the RCMP and the media.)
